explica.AL1: you do it yourself; AI is not involved.
explica.AL2: AI helps: you ask, it answers, you do the work.
explica.AL3: AI collaborates: you work together, and you lead each step.
explica.AL4: AI leads and you review before it goes out.
explica.AL5: AI runs on its own, with a schedule, rules, and an alarm.

o_que_subir.AL2: Start asking AI before doing the work by hand. There is no threshold: the risk is low.
o_que_subir.AL3: Give AI the fixed context (instructions, examples, where the files are) and work together. Ready when 10 consecutive runs need no more than 1 major correction.
o_que_subir.AL4: Let AI prepare everything and just review before it goes out. Ready when, out of 20 runs, no more than 2 need a major correction.
o_que_subir.AL5: Put it on a timer, with a limit, an alarm, and a way to undo it. Only when, out of 50 runs, no more than 2 need a major correction and none has a serious error.

rel.curta: Attention: you requested {dias} days, but the {fonte} records cover only {n} days (since {desde}). For {fonte}, the result applies only to that period. Claude Code deletes records older than 30 days unless you increase cleanupPeriodDays; anything already deleted cannot be recovered.
rel.conduz: AI leads **{pct}%** of the measured work (AL4 + AL5)
rel.tab_escada: Level | What it means | Share of time
rel.al1_zero: AL1 is at 0% because work you do without AI does not appear in the logs. Record it on the paper sheet (registro/papel.csv) to include it in the totals.
rel.tab_tarefas: Task | h/week | Runs | Level | Next step
rel.atencao: Attention: a critical task is running on its own
rel.atencao_linha: - **{tarefa}**: {pct}% of the time at AL5. Critical tasks stop at AL4: check that there is a review, an alarm, and a way back.
rel.descer: Go down one level (and record the new level from now on)
rel.subir: You can go up one level now (the sheet criteria are met)
rel.candidatas: Candidates for moving up: accuracy still needs to be measured
rel.quem_decide: You decide. The program measures how much freedom AI had; whether it got things right is shown only by the sheet columns "fixed?" and "serious error".
rel.tab_conexoes: Connection | Sessions | Uses | First | Last | On its own
rel.fontes: {claude} Claude Code sessions and {codex} Codex sessions: {conversas} conversations with you and {sozinhas} that ran on their own; {acoes} AI actions, {externos} with an effect outside the machine (publishing, sending, uploading). Paper sheet rows: {papel}.
rel.tempo_nota: Time means work time WITH AI (parallel sessions are added together). Use it to compare tasks, not to count your hours.
rel.nivel_nota: The level shows how much freedom AI had, not whether it got things right. Accuracy is the sheet's "fixed?" column.
